newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds track U.S. treasuries higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds track U.S. treasuries higher.

text.p: Argentine bonds firmed Tuesday on higher U.S. treasury bonds, and aided by an expanded global bond placement, traders said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.40 to 118.40, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 5/8 to 84-3/8.
"The bond market is still basically firm, but it is likely that there may be some light profit-taking in the next few days," one trader said.
"External factors are positive, and added to the good response in foreign markets to the launch of Argentina's global bond it makes for an encouraging situation for the investor," he added.
The Economy Ministry said Tuesday that Argentina will expand its global bond issue to $1 billion from an originally-scheduled $750 million due to an "excellent response" from financial markets.
The 10-year bonds are being placed at between 445-450 basis points above the 10-year U.S. treasury note. The bond's pricing is set for Wednesday.
But one analyst said that the market was not as impressed as it might have been with the global bond: "The spread was seen a little bit wide, but nothing out of ordinary."
He said, "We're basically tracking the U.S. treasury. But then there was this last U.S. rally the market here did not follow too much.
"I'd say we're in a trading range, as the U.S. treasury seems to be. As the market approaches 85 for the FRB, it just loses strength."
Interbank call money closed up at 6.8 percent from 5.975 percent at close Monday.
